proposition.claim:
The definition requiring pi_1(Lbar)=G does not yield a finite C_{1,1}(G) for general finitely generated hyperbolic groups.

One subdivision need not make the quotient simplicial; an ordinary undirected Cayley action with involutions is not free on the realization.

The subgroup index formula used in the proof applies to k nonzero, not every integer k.

The full Rips target need not have dimension m; the Section8 application omits the standard instruction to use its m-skeleton and the corresponding cellular extension.

repair.content:
Restrict the rank comparison to nontrivial free groups, or separately define the m=1 action-based complexity. Explicitly use m>=2 for the main invariant.

Choose a finite genuine simplicial presentation complex P for G and let X' be the one-skeleton of its universal cover. The deck action is free and cocompact, X'/G=P^(1) is simplicial, X' is quasi-isometric to G, and Vol(X'/H)=[G:H]Vol(X'/G) for every finite-index H. Thus the conclusion of Theorem C is unchanged, with constants depending on the fixed model.

State m,n in Z minus {0}, or add the Euler-characteristic argument for zero powers. Clarify whether the notation denotes the cyclic subgroup or a mapping torus with an abstract infinite cyclic factor.

Specify Z=Y_full^(m) and choose the equivariant cellular extension relative to the selected geodesic edges. Apply Proposition7.1 to Z; its conclusion on the common1-skeleton gives the needed estimate with constants dependingonlyon thefixedtarget. No newgroupassumption or asymptotic bound. The prior full-target vanishing/naturality proof remains a valid alternative.
